replacedBy.note: In the DeepSeek API: V4-Flash was retired on 2026-09-10 and deepseek-v4-flash temporarily routes to DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash.

summary.text: DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731 is the official, non-preview release of DeepSeek-V4-Flash, with open weights under the MIT License, served in the DeepSeek API from 2026-07-31 under the unchanged name deepseek-v4-flash. DeepSeek says it keeps the preview's architecture and size and differs in renewed post-training. It was retired in the API on 2026-09-10.

features.note: Reasoning effort levels low, high and max; thinking and non-thinking modes in the API.

inputModalities.note: The API lists vision as not supported for deepseek-v4-pro.

sources.locator: Model Details: Features, Vision not supported

openWeights.note: Weights under the MIT License.

changes.text: Adds an attached DSpark speculative decoding module on top of the preview's model structure.
Natively supports the OpenAI Responses API format, adapted for Codex with a one-click setup script.
DeepSeek reports improved agent capabilities over the preview, especially in production environments.
Released together with peak and off-peak API prices, with off-peak at half the peak rate, effective 2026-08-16 at 16:00 UTC.

lifecycle.note: Served in the DeepSeek API as deepseek-v4-pro on 2026-10-01; weights downloadable from Hugging Face. The V4.1-Flash news post announced that deepseek-v4-pro requests would route to V4.1-Flash from 2026-09-14, but the change log entry of the same day says the V4 Pro API continues after 2026-09-14, and the pricing page still lists DeepSeek-V4-Pro-0813.

summary.text: DeepSeek-V4-Pro-0813 is the general-availability release of DeepSeek-V4-Pro, rolled out on 2026-08-13 in the DeepSeek app, web chat (Expert Mode) and API under the unchanged name deepseek-v4-pro, with weights under the MIT License. It keeps the preview's model structure and adds a DSpark speculative decoding module; DeepSeek describes much stronger agent capabilities.

features.note: The card reports evaluating it at the max reasoning effort level.

openWeights.note: Repository licensed under the MIT License; weight shards published on Hugging Face after the API release.

changes.text: Adds image input next to text; images can be sent as base64, as external URLs or through the new Files API.
Adds visual modules to the V4-Flash architecture, followed by continued training.
Offered only in the DeepSeek API at launch, as an experimental model; the weights followed later on Hugging Face.

released.note: API release; the weights appeared on Hugging Face later (repository created 2026-08-31 according to hub metadata; no page states the date).

lifecycle.note: Weights downloadable from the deepseek-ai Hugging Face organisation. In the DeepSeek API the model was retired on 2026-09-10; the legacy name deepseek-v4-flash-vision-exp now routes to DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash.

relations.note: The card says it builds on the DeepSeek-V4-Flash architecture by adding visual modules and continued training. It does not name the starting checkpoint; the card compares it with DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731 and the change log with the official DeepSeek-V4-Flash, so that revision is a possible alternative target.

replacedBy.note: In the DeepSeek API: retired on 2026-09-10; deepseek-v4-flash-vision-exp temporarily routes to DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash.

summary.text: DeepSeek-V4-Flash-Vision-Exp is an experimental model that DeepSeek calls its first multimodal model in the DeepSeek-V4 family, built on the V4-Flash architecture with added visual modules. It accepted text and images in the DeepSeek API from 2026-08-21, later got open weights under the MIT License and was retired in the API on 2026-09-10.

features.note: Continuously controllable reasoning effort (1 to 100) in the open model; thinking and non-thinking modes in the API.

openWeights.note: Weights under the MIT License.

parameters.note: Mixture-of-Experts with 552B backbone parameters; 8B activated per token during prefill (input) and 16B during decode (output). The card also lists an Engram conditional memory of 196B parameters among additional components; whether it is counted in the 552B is not stated.

changes.text: Processes images natively together with text, trained jointly from the start of pre-training; the previous Flash model accepted text only.
Switches to a Causal Encoder-Decoder design with 8B active parameters for input and 16B for output, plus CSA2 sparse attention and Engram conditional memory.
Trained from scratch on a 45T-token multimodal corpus, rather than derived from a V4 checkpoint.
According to DeepSeek, its KV cache needs about a quarter of the HBM and an eighth of the SSD storage of the previous generation.

news.title: DeepSeek V4.1 Flash: Two Rates for One Model, and a Legacy Id That Now Serves Another

relations.note: The change log calls V4 Flash and V4 Flash Vision Exp the previous-generation models, retired with this release, and routes their API names to V4.1-Flash; at that point deepseek-v4-flash served DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731 (change log, 2026-07-31).

summary.text: DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash is a Mixture-of-Experts model with 552B backbone parameters that takes text and images and generates text, released on 2026-09-10 in the DeepSeek API as deepseek-flash and with open weights under the MIT License. DeepSeek calls it the smallest model of a new architecture family and says it was trained from scratch.

news.title: DeepSeek V4.1 Flash: Two Rates for One Model, and a Legacy Id That Now Serves Another

description.text: DeepSeek (Hangzhou DeepSeek Artificial Intelligence Co., Ltd.) is a Chinese AI company that says it was founded in 2023. It describes itself as a research team focused on fundamental model research with an open-source approach, and says it releases model weights under the MIT License with a technical report for each model. It offers its models through a web chat, mobile apps and an API platform.
